sciparseR was designed after reviewing the existing tools for parsing
scientific documents. This article records what each one does, its
license, and how sciparseR relates to it. Licenses were read from the
projects' license files in November 2026.

| Project | Language | License | Relation to sciparseR |
|---|---|---|---|
| pdftools (poppler) | R, C++ | MIT | Required. Word boxes, fonts, metadata, page rendering. |
| xml2 (libxml2) | R, C | MIT | Required. JATS parsing. |
| jsonlite, digest | R | MIT, GPL-2+ | Required. Serialization and checksums. |
| tesseract | R, C++ | Apache-2.0 | Optional OCR. |
| ellmer | R | MIT | Optional language model engine (all providers). |
| ellmercodex | R | MIT | Optional ChatGPT plan provider for ellmer. |
| nativeORT | R, C++ | MIT | Optional ONNX inference (raw). |
| arrow | R, C++ | Apache-2.0 | Optional Parquet export. |
| tabulapdf | R, Java | Apache-2.0 | Not used: needs Java. Comparable table extraction. |
| JATSdecoder | R | GPL-3 | Not used, no code reused. Extracts text and statistics from JATS. |
| tableParser | R | GPL-3 | Not used, no code reused. Statistics from HTML and XML tables. |
| doclingr / Docling | R wrapper, Python | MIT | Not used: Python. Comparison target. |
| GROBID | Java service | Apache-2.0 | Optional comparison through its TEI output. |
| Marker | Python | Apache-2.0 code, OpenRAIL-M weights | Comparison target. |
| MinerU | Python | Apache-2.0 with additional terms | Comparison target. |
| olmOCR | Python | Apache-2.0 | Comparison target (needs a GPU). |
| Table Transformer | Python | MIT | Candidate ONNX table model; not integrated in this version. |
| PyMuPDF4LLM | Python | AGPL-3 | Not used. |

## What is different

Each of these tools does part of the job well. sciparseR's aim is a
combination that none of the R packages offers:

* **One model for PDF and JATS.** The same accessors, extraction,
  validation and exports work for both sources.
* **Provenance everywhere.** Every element has a page and box or an
  XPath, a method and a status; every extracted value has evidence with
  the exact text, character offsets and the document checksum.
* **Explicit uncertainty.** Statuses distinguish reported, missing, not
  reported, ambiguous and unsupported values, and data origins distinguish
  reported, derived, model inferred and human corrected values.
* **Native and offline by default.** No Java, Python, GPU or network for
  the core. Optional tools are used only when asked for.

## Where Python tools are stronger

Deep learning pipelines such as Docling, Marker and MinerU recognize
layouts, complex tables and formulas that geometric methods cannot
(tables without aligned columns, tables as images, LaTeX from formula
images). For such documents, use them alongside sciparseR, or use the
publisher's JATS when it exists. `sc_evaluate()` scores an
`sc_document` against a ground truth file; the output of another parser
can be scored after it is converted to an `sc_document` (GROBID TEI with
`sc_read_grobid()`).
